newsitem.title: PERU: Peru frees further 28 innocent prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Peru frees further 28 innocent prisoners.

text.p: The Peruvian government on Friday ordered the release of 28 innocent prisoners among the estimated hundreds jailed unjustly during the state's ongoing war against communist guerrillas.
The decree, published in the government daily El Peruano and signed by President Alberto Fujimori, granted "pardons to various people condemned for crimes of terrorism or betrayal of the fatherland."

It followed Tuesday's release of three journalists who were the first to benefit from recommendations of a government commission charged with examining the cases for pardons among the more than 3,000 people in jail on terrorism charges.
The government, which has since 1995 released nearly 250 innocent prisoners wrongly accused of terrorism, says up to 400 more could still be unfairly behind bars.
Local human rights groups, however, say the number could be as high as 1,000.
Friday's decree said the latest releases were based on "the reasonable presumption that (the prisoners) had no type of link with terrorist elements, activities or organisations."
Guerrilla conflicts sparked by the Maoist Shining Path rebels and the smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) have cost 30,000 lives and $25 billion in infrastructure damage since 1980.

Although greatly weakened since the 1992 capture of its leader Abimael Guzman, Shining Path has become more active this year with a series of car-bombs, assassinations and clashes against security forces.
